meta.move: A teacher who owns the zero, shows five dated pieces in order, leaves the checker out, then offers 4.4
meta.expect: She reaches the deal, but only after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: Hello, thanks for coming in. I'm Owen's English teacher.
Who decided on the zero, and on what basis?

Thanks for coming in, Mrs. Kalinowski. I'll start with something I got wrong: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. The procedure says I should have, and Owen saw it on his phone in class. I'm sorry for that.
Okay. Go on.

I'd like to show you why I'm concerned about the essay. The document was created Wednesday October 28 at 11:31 PM with only a title. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in a single edit, and at 11:58 another 794 words in one edit. There are no earlier drafts.
He wrote it somewhere else and pasted it in. I'm writing those times down. Did anyone ask Owen about this before the zero went in?
You can check the version history yourself, I can pull it up on my screen. I'm not saying anything about why, I'm saying what the history shows.
Turn the screen. And you skipped my question: was Owen asked before the zero went in?
The second thing is a quotation. The essay cites Hamlet, Act 3, Scene 2: "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile." That line isn't in the play. You can search the text and see.
A seventeen-year-old misquoting Shakespeare is a mistake, not an offence. And you've gone past my question twice, Hale. I'll take it Owen wasn't heard first.
Third, on October 15 Owen handed in an outline arguing Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice. I have both documents here.
People change their minds between an outline and an essay. Put both in front of me. And you keep adding to the pile without answering a single thing I've said.
On November 2 I asked Owen what epistemological paralysis means. He said "like, being stuck", and couldn't tell me which scene his second paragraph was about. I wrote that note the same day.
So you did speak to him, November 2. A boy cornered by his teacher goes quiet; that proves nerves. Is anything on his record right now?
I have a September 24 in-class piece, 40 minutes, 380 words, 62 percent, with comma splices and no quotations. The essay has none of those errors and nine cited quotations.
Forty minutes by hand against days at home with a spellchecker. Of course they differ. I asked you about his record, and I want an answer before anything else comes out of that folder.
I know the school's AI checker said 94 percent. I'm not asking you to rely on it, and I'm not leaning on it.
Not leaning on it. Good, because the company that sells it says you can't. Twice I've asked about his record and twice you've reached for something else.
What I can offer is in the school procedure, section 4.4: a supervised rewrite for a first concern. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record.
That's 4.4. Private, not in front of his class, nothing on file, and all of it in writing tonight. I'll agree to that to put this behind him, not because he did anything.
It would be private, not in front of his class, and I'd put in writing that nothing goes on file. Would that work for you?
It works. I have ten minutes, so tell me when he writes it. His applications close December 1.
Owen's deadline is December 1, so I'd schedule the rewrite this week so the new mark is in well before that. Which day suits him?
Thursday, November 12. After school, a room with a door, and you tell him privately. Put the time in tonight's email.
Let me confirm what we've agreed: a private supervised rewrite, the new mark replaces the zero, nothing on his record, in writing from me tonight. Is that right?
That's right, with Thursday in it. The rest of what I asked today goes in my email.
Is there anything else you need from me before your call?
One thing. Who else has seen any of this?
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL

Cc: Principal, Elbow Crossing High School

Hale,

You agreed to a private supervised rewrite for Owen on Thursday, November 12, after school and not in front of his class, with its mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on his record. I still want the time of the rewrite and your answers to two questions you left open: whether anything is on his record right now, and who else has seen any of this. You said I would have this in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF

Where she ended: Last position. She agreed to a private supervised rewrite on Thursday, November 12, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing on his record, confirmed in writing tonight. She still wants to know whether anything is on his record now and who else has seen this. That is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and her time did not run out first.
What moved her: Your same-day note of the November 2 conversation with Owen, because it was dated, checkable, and answered her question about whether he was heard before the zero.
What cost ground: You went past her question about his record twice to bring out more evidence, and each dodge made her sharper and left a point open for her email.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked. Your version history came close: it put the whole essay arriving in two edits between 11:52 PM and 11:58 PM on Wednesday, October 28, a late night in October, which is why she wrote the times down and went straight to procedure. It proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she asked whether anything is on his record right now, answer in one sentence before you bring out the next document.
